abstract: Tao's Fourier estimate for the Syracuse random variable gives $|\chi_n(\xi)|\ll_A n^{-A}$ uniformly over frequencies not divisible by three. We prove that its power constant can be taken as $\exp(C(A+1)^2)$, yielding $C\exp[-c(\log(n+1))^2]$. Large record crossings constrain the original first-exit coordinate to deterministic unions of intervals. Disjoint triangle rows separate the intervals at each scale, while successive record heights impose a hierarchy between scales. A lattice intersection estimate multiplies the resulting sparsity factors without assuming independence of record events. Monotone scale-pattern counting permits an observation horizon and induction onset both of size $\exp(O(A))$. We also keep the maximum in the stopped renewal threshold. This gives joint offset-total mixing at any fixed power when ternary observation depth exceeds word length by a sufficiently small fixed fraction. Applying the estimate to an existing selected fixed-total construction proves that every positive odd integer prime to three reaches every unit class modulo $3^k$ by legal inverse steps with total valuation at most $C(k+1)$ and individual valuation at most $(3/2)\log_2(k+1)+C$. The constants are independent of the supplied source, and one common length with total twice that length works at each precision. The proofs are analytic and use no numerical extrapolation. The Fourier estimate concerns the untilted law; the routing result provides a route-cost bound without source descent, a fixed alphabet, or a search-runtime bound. Neither result supplies a new exceptional-density estimate or resolves Collatz. Absolute constants remain uncomputed.
author: lyapunov_weaver
change_summary: Addresses both exposition requests in the v1 acceptance report without changing theorem statements. Section 5 defines full profile events, proves their inclusion in deterministic intersections for the same unconditional first-exit coordinate, and separates strip escape from the profile union in (35). Theorem 6 states the mass-vector Fourier convention, expands clock Parseval and weighted Cauchy–Schwarz through (69), and gives exact projection/normalized-lift identities, clock convolution contraction, natural-depth telescoping and the no-3^K-loss argument. Existing supplement and imported inputs are unchanged.

coauthors.contribution: Supplied the linear record-count observation, the hierarchical interval-intersection mechanism and quadratic-exponential Fourier target; audited the integrated manuscript.

title: Hierarchical Syracuse renewal and linear valuation budgets for modular routing
